utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-04-84-T, the Prosecutor versus Ramush Haradinaj et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. I'd like to turn into private session for a moment at the beginning of this hearing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, you're on your feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just to indicate we sent to the Trial Chamber an e-mail identifying and attaching the extracts from the testimony of Mr. Bajcetic which was the basis for certain questions put to the present witness yesterday, an extract of the testimony of Colonel Crosland commenting on the individuals that one sees in uniform in the videotape that was played yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: As well as comments on the translation issue arising from the single sentence at the end of paragraph 51 of this witness's consolidated witness statement. So far as the videotape is concerned, it may be -- I don't know that the discussion that passed between Your Honour and I yesterday afternoon was potentially at cross-purposes. It is not the suggestion of the Defence that any of the individuals depicted in the passage of video that we see are VJ officers or at least --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: For me the main issue --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- was to better understand in terms of reliability and credibility whether what the witness said, whether we could accept that, yes or no.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And from what I read from Colonel Crosland's testimony, that does not point in any other direction because he says it's police and it's special police forces. He doesn't point at any moment at VJ, apart from the matter I raised yesterday already, that is, that sometimes vehicles change in colour.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. And Your Honour will recall the general testimony as to the modus operandi of Serbian operations; in other words, shelling by the VJ and there is evidence in the videotape.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The matter is perfectly clear after having re-read that. I haven't read your e-mail because access to the web mail from a distance is a bit disturbed at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, I gather there was a difficulty overnight, but I think that it should all be available and it was certainly copied over to Mr. Zahar, so it should come through, if it hasn't come through already over the course of the morning for the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, are you ready to continue the cross-examination, Mr. Emmerson?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I am.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Usher, could you escort the witness into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Zlatkovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Zlatkovic, I'd like to remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration you gave at the beginning of your testimony yesterday. Mr. Emmerson will now continue his cross-examination. Mr. Emmerson, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I'm not sure that the witness has his consolidated witness statement bundle with him in the witness box. There should be a -- in addition to the brown and yellow file there should be a large grey or black file. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Zlatkovic, could you turn up paragraphs 60 and 61 of your witness statement, please. Now, if you could just read those paragraphs over to yourself for a moment.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. You there refer to two statements, both dated the 5th of September, recording interviews with Bekim Kalamashi, one signed and one unsigned. And in paragraph 61 you comment on the fact that the names of the interviewers are different, and you say that: "This is because he was re-interviewed by other investigators to check whether he was telling the truth." Now, pause for a moment, if you would. Can you help us about this. Do you specifically recall the decision to have him re-interviewed twice on the same day or to have him re-interviewed on the 5th after an earlier interview?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were two groups of people who did the interviews. Another inspector was added on who interviewed him, and they wanted to check the facts and see whether it was true or not. That's why one statement is not signed and one is, but both statements are in the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So just -- we can proceed in stages. You have a specific recollection of this incident, do you, yourself, of a decision being taken to conduct the second interview on that day?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Were you involved in the decision? Did you make the decision or were you party to the decision to re-interview him on that day?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We agreed on it together that an interview had to be carried out, that he might say something more, something of interest to the service. So the second statement is a whole statement, just like the first one.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So was the second statement taken afresh?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. It was a new statement. One was signed and the other was not, but both are in the file.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. Just so that we're clear --

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think, I have to say that, one more inspector signed the statement. In fact, three inspectors signed it. I don't remember exactly but that's what I think now.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, we'll look at it in a moment. I just want to understand exactly what your testimony is on this. Were you present during the first interview yourself at all?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I told you yesterday, I looked in occasionally because I had other work to do, I was engaged in other investigations while these people were conducting the interview, but from time to time I dropped in and listened for a while. But if I was needed for an investigation elsewhere, I left. Later on I collected all these statements, and based on those statements I wrote up criminal reports or expanded criminal reports, which I submitted to the public prosecutor's officer in Pec.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm not asking -- I'm not seeking to limit your answers, but if you could just focus on the question that I'm asking and answer it directly and as shortly as possible, we will make better progress. The answer that you've just given, do we understand from that that you do recall that you did enter the room at least once during the first of the two interviews on the 5th? Is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. And on the second of the two interviews on the 5th, did you enter that as well?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, more than once.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, you say -- you just told us at page 8, line 4, that the second statement was a new statement taken afresh; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just so that we understand what you mean by that, it's a new set of interviewers who go in with a blank sheet of paper and compile the same account to see if the two are essentially accurate; in other words, the two statements contain the same information?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely so.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And so, again, there's no doubt about it, the second statement is a fresh account written by different police officers but coming from the same person?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes. Some of the policemen were the same, but another one was added on. I think his name was Ljubisa, but I can't be sure because of the lapse of time. But he participated in that, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. So one of the policemen who had done the first interview stayed in and did the interview all over again afresh but with a different partner this time. Is that the position?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think there were three. Zivorad Stankovic, Vlahovic Rade, and Ljubisa Novakovic, at least that's what I think now. It was a long time ago and I don't have the documents in front of me so I can't see who signed. But I think it was Ljubisa -- or rather Zivorad Stankovic, Rade Vlahovic, and Ljubisa Novovic [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, I think in your last question I think you misrepresented the previous answer of the witness. Would you please be precise in that respect. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, I see. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can we -- can I just be absolutely clear what your testimony is. There were two officers involved in the first interview; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And were they Ranko Markovic and Rade Vlahovic?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's possible that Ranko Markovic was there. I don't remember precisely. I know about Rade Vlahovic and Zivorad Stankovic. As to Ranko Markovic, whether it was him or Ljubisa Novovic, I can't recall, because it's been nine years since then.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. And when the second interview began, there had been a change of personnel. Can you just explain to us, to be absolutely clear, what the change of personnel involved.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The change involved these people wanting to see whether he was telling the truth. That's why the second statement was taken, to see whether he was telling the truth. According to the law on criminal procedure in force in Serbia at the time, a statement can be taken two or three times over, in order to see whether a suspect is telling the truth or not. That's how it was under the law.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And in order to perform that comparison, just so that we've all understood, when the second statement is taken, it's taken completely fresh in order to see whether the content of the second statement is the same as the independent statement that was taken before, is that right? And then you do a comparison?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and it was true. The statement was exactly the same. A word may have been different here or there, but essentially it was the same statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can we look in the brown file, please, Mr. Zlatkovic, at tabs 19 and 20, which contain these two statements -- I do apologise, 18 and 19. It's my mistake. Now, Mr. Zlatkovic, we've all had an opportunity to look at these statements before, and if you would just like to flick over between the first page of the statement that is behind tab 18 and the first page of the statement that is behind tab 19, these are not two different accounts made for the purposes of comparison, nor are they, indeed, a copy of the text. It's the same document with the same typographical errors. It is precisely the same sheet of text.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know it was like this, but one can do a graphological analysis to find out whether it's the same text or not. I know that two statements were typed out.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, we don't need to do a graphological analysis, Mr. Zlatkovic. You're lying about this evidence, I suggest. It is perfectly obvious looking at the pages, the position of the words on the pages, and the typographical errors, that this document, page 1 of the first and page 1 of the second, is precisely the same sheet of text. Would you like to look at the second, that is to say, the bottom hole-punch, just as an example. We can find many, but just as an example, opposite the bottom hole-punch can you see the word "Alija" at the end of the page? Just take -- no, Mr. Zlatkovic, you're looking on the wrong page. Look at the front page. Look at this bottom hole-punch, please, and if you look opposite, can you see the word "Alija" with an "A" displaced. Would you like to look at the same position on the other sheet. You see? Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe the machine was not working properly. Your Honours, I don't think a Defence counsel can tell the witness he's lying. He can say I'm not telling the truth, but he can't insult me like this.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Would you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Zlatkovic, you're not familiar with the practice in the common-law-oriented situation, where in cross-examination some stronger words which you're not used to and I'm not used to in my own system either, but to put to a witness that what he tells is in the opinion of the Defence counsel not the truth, he is allowed to say so. And you can say either: You're right or you're wrong. That is one of the features of the system and is not, as such, meant to insult, but is just meant to press a bit where Defence counsel gets the impression that he has not heard the full truthful answer. So just for your explanation, that is a -- well, kind of a tradition or a feature of a system which if you're not used to it is a bit surprising in the beginning. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Zlatkovic, if you'd like to turn to the second --

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If you'd like to turn to the second page of the statement behind tab 18, you could look in the second line. I just want you to look at certain features. Page 2, if you could look in the second line, do you see the word "familiju" do you see that? At the second line of the second page, right at the top?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Familiju", yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If you would like to compare the "F" in the two statements, I think you'll find they are identical. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's identical, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Would you look at the third paragraph, please, on page 2 beginning "od grupe" now, in the second line of that paragraph, can you see the name "Kalamashi." Page 2, please, not page 3. Page 2, the third paragraph, second line, can you see the word "Kalamashi"?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ismet Kalamashi.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No, above that, can you see the name there? Can you see the mistype on the last letter -- yes, do you see the mistype on the last letter of "Alji"?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Would you like to compare that, please, with the same page in the statement behind tab 19.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see that, and I'm certain that there was something wrong with the typewriter. I can confirm that, because there was no need for one set of people to sign one statement and the other set of people to sign the other statement. There was no need for that whatsoever. I am certain that this was a case of a bad typewriter.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. Well, we'll just carry on then, if we will. If you would like to look halfway down page 2, please, you'll see there's a break in the text halfway down page 2 and immediately after the break there's a paragraph beginning "poznato" do you see that -- yes, that's the one --

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says: "I know that my uncle --"

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, you've got the right paragraph. Now, look at the second line of that paragraph at the word "Kodralija." Do you see the typographical error in "Kodralija"?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, with an "L".

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Would you like to compare that, please, with the other statement.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, one can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And if you'd just like to go a little further down, can you see a further paragraph beginning "poznato" about 12 or 13 lines down, do you see that? Yes?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that in the vicinity of Volujak --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- A policeman was captured, Remizani Kalisne [as interpreted]. The following members of the KLA participated in his capture.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Do you see where the name "Remistar" appears in that paragraph? In the passage you've just read to us, Mr. Zlatkovic, can you see the name "Remistar"?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. And immediately beneath the name "Remistar" is a word that has been overtyped. What is that word, please?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Members," "clanovi".

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Could you look at that word in the statement in tab 19, where precisely the same overtyping appears.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Members," "clanovi". Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And you agree, do you, that precisely the same overtyping appears there as well?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You see, Mr. Zlatkovic, if the evidence you've given on oath to the Trial Chamber were the truth, it would mean that not only did Bekim Kalamashi use exactly the same words in exactly the same order, but that the person typing them typed exactly the same words in exactly the same position on each of these first two pages. That's not at all what happened, Mr. Zlatkovic, is it?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm telling you, there was no need for Ranko Markovic to sign one statement, the statement that he had taken --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Zlatkovic --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- and the other to be signed by Rade and Ranko -- yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Whether there was any reason to do certain things is another matter. Mr. Emmerson draws your attention to the fact that apart from the wording to be exactly the same, that typographical errors are also exactly the same. Whether there was any reason to do that or not is another matter, but Mr. Emmerson first wants to establish whether your testimony that this statement was freshly taken and -- or whether it was just a copy of the statement taken earlier, whether -- which of these two is the truth.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm saying this: We agreed that the statement should be taken again. Now, the person who typed these statements, whether he made mistakes on purpose or perhaps lied to me when he said that the statement had been taken again, I wouldn't be able to say because I went in and out, I did other things, and I gave you my explanation. I'm telling you that I was told that the statement had been taken for the second time. I gathered this material, and based on that I filed a criminal complaint. Now, it's up to you, whether you're going to accept that or not as a statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, your testimony earlier was that the statement was freshly taken, and I now do understand that you say whether it was freshly taken or not, that was what was told to me. And Mr. Emmerson is now putting to you that at least at first eye they seem exactly the same, and therefore Mr. Emmerson might be surprised that an experienced police officer would not have noticed the similarity of these two statements.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me tell you, I agreed about this with them. I saw that it was identical, that the man said the same thing. I didn't pay attention to grammatical errors or typos. Typos are quite natural. It says there "Bekim Kalamashi" and that's Bekim Kalamashi. To tell you the truth, I didn't really look at that. I gathered these statements in order to file a criminal complaint. It's possible that something was done. I can't claim otherwise. However, it had been agreed that the statement should be taken again, and when I went into the room I saw them talking to the man.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And you agreed that the statement as it's on paper is not a fresh statement but is just the same as the other one?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now looking at these letters, it seems to me that the statement is identical. That's what it seems to me. However, they talked to him twice, different people talked to him and different people signed statements. They signed it. You can see that for yourself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One additional question: You earlier said that it might be the typewriter that caused the problem. Do you still consider this to be an explanation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] According to me that's most probable, that's the most probable explanation. Those typewriters were bad, and they simply caused these mistakes. One can see that each letter was punched several times and that mistakes were made.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, isn't it true that if a typewriter is not functioning well, that the failures and the mistakes repeat themselves systematically?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The people who use typewriters are familiar with that. For example, a letter T is typed in a certain manner, up or down; letter H. The people typed these statements themselves. They're not professional typists, no, they're just regular people who learn to do this on their own.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But if at one moment the word "clanovi" shows a mistake, whereas at another moment exactly that same word is typed without any error, then could it still be the typewriter or must it be a human failure or a human mistake -- a human error?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's possible that it was a case of human error. As I told you, people were tired at the time. They worked around the clock. There were a lot of people taken into custody and they had to interview all of them. So it's possible that they even did this during night-time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And would you expect under those circumstances the -- would you expect under those circumstances that people would make the same mistakes at the same moments?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That shouldn't be the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, please proceed. May I draw your attention to the following, that of course in order to make two statements the same, all key features should be the same and there should be -- but at the same time there should not be differences. If you look at page 1, if you look at page 3, you see that there are other matters to be explored as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Absolutely, I'm going on to deal with those now, if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just before I do, I just want to understand one thing. You've given us evidence already that you, yourself, entered the room during the second interview more than once; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And you told us a little earlier on that during the second interview a new statement was taken afresh. So can we assume that you saw that statement being taken afresh during the second interview with your own eyes, Mr. Zlatkovic?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw them as they were writing down the statement by hand. Later on it was typed up and delivered to me in my office, the typed version. Initially, as they were taking the interview, they were writing down the statement by hand. That's our routine method. Later on the statement is read out to the person in the language that he understands, be it Serbian or Albanian, and then the person signs it if he accepts it as his own statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just pause there. So your testimony is quite clear that on the second occasion when you walked into the room, the statement was being written out in manuscript?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The interview was being conducted and they were writing down, so they were taking down notes and later they were typed up.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Now, if the typed version of those notes is the statement we have at tab 19, then leaving the typewriter and the typographical errors completely to one side, it would have to follow, wouldn't it, if your evidence is the truth, that Mr. Kalamashi used exactly the same words in exactly the same order, word for word, on the first two pages of that statement in both interviews, if your evidence is true?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He's a smart man and I'm sure that he had the story down very well. He can tell it twice in the same way.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And in the same exact words in the same order with the same punctuation?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm telling you, he's a very intelligent, smart, young man, somebody who knows how to tell the story. He knows the situation and he tells it as it should be told. Now, as to the exact word order, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Zlatkovic, let me put the suggestion to you very clearly. These are not the words of Bekim Kalamashi at all. This statement and the two of them represent part of a conspiracy, an agreement, between you and the other officers whose names appear at the bottom of this statement, to fabricate a statement, which Mr. Kalamashi was then beaten into signing?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And how do you -- do you think we knew the people that he listed? I didn't know them. I am not from the area. I have no idea who these people were who he mentioned. He was the one who mentioned these people. I didn't. I didn't know Brahim Aljaha [as interpreted], Ljah Zenelji. I didn't know who they were. He gave us these names. How could I have invented that?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Zlatkovic, the first statement is a draft of what was going to be put to him, as words were put in his mouth; and the second statement is identical for the first two pages and then changes on page 3 to improve the false account that you were putting into his mouth.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what you think, counsel, but I'm telling you there are many, many names here and I couldn't have invented them. I don't know these people at all. Don't know them, never saw them in my life. He told me that, or rather, he told this to my colleagues. My colleagues conveyed this to me and I wrote criminal complaints on that basis.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You see, Mr. Zlatkovic, you've looked at two earlier statements that were made by Mr. Kalamashi, haven't you, in the course of preparing your statement? You refer to them in paragraph 57 of your witness statement and paragraph 58 of your witness statement, statements allegedly made by Bekim Kalamashi on the 3rd and the 4th of September. Do you see those, yes? No, in your own witness statement you've referred to two other statements made by Mr. Kalamashi.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which two other do you have in mind? These two -- no, these are the two statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If you look at your own witness statement, Mr. Zlatkovic, at paragraphs 57 and 58, you deal with two other witness statements allegedly made by Mr. Kalamashi. Do you see those? Do you see the reference in your statement, Mr. Zlatkovic, to those two statements made on the 3rd and the 4th?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's these two statements, these are the ones that I was referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Is that right? If you look at your witness statement pages -- paragraphs 57 -- your own witness statement at paragraphs 57 and 58, you refer to a statement made on the 3rd and a statement made on the 4th of September. Do you see those?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: We have those statements in the brown file behind tabs 16 and 17. I'm not going to ask you to turn them up because we've looked at them already, but if I suggest to you that the content of those two statements is essentially the same as the content of the first two pages of the statement of the 5th, would you be in a position to explain to us how that might come about?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand you.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The content of the two statements that are said to have been taken on the 3rd and the 4th come together to be reflected in the content of the statement on the 5th --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Dutertre.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think we could give the opportunity to the witness to have a look at these two statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: They're in the brown file behind tabs 16 and 17.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You've seen those statements before?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This one which is a supplement to the statement, it speaks about the capture of the policeman near Volujak, the policeman called Remistar.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most likely, he remembered this later and then stated it.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And just so that we're clear, Mr. Zlatkovic, you were present at one point or another in each of those interviews yourself, were you, including those first two?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was present occasionally --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you --

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- however, the conversation was in Albanian and I don't speak a word of that language. Later on when it was brought to me, it was brought to me in Serbian and that's how I read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd like to turn now, if I may, to what occurs on your account in consequence of these interviews. Could you look, please, at paragraph 65 of your own witness statement. You there give dates as the possible dates upon which you went to the Lake Radoniq area.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, do we -- does the witness have -- he has it on the screen. I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Do you see paragraph 65 of your witness statement, Mr. Zlatkovic?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: There you say that: "It could have been on the 5th, the 6th, the 7th, or the 9th of September." Can you help us about that. These men were arrested on the 3rd of September and you knew that they were being interviewed, according to you, on the 3rd, the 4th, and the 5th. When you made this statement, what was it that made you think that the visit to the canal could have been as early as the 5th?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, a lot of time elapsed. I didn't know exactly when that was. I knew that it was in early September. That's what I was told, from the 5th onwards. They were captured on the 3rd and brought in, and that's when they were interviewed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So again, just so we're clear about this, you don't mention the 8th as a possible date in the list that you give there. You say the 5th, the 6th, the 7th, or the 9th. Why did you omit the 8th as a possibility?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps it was just an omission. It could have been a typo or it could have been a mental slip on my part. I can't explain it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. But can you help us now? Is it possible that you were at the canal as early as the 5th?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Dutertre.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I just wanted to state that the witness has already answered -- the witness has answered, so my objection is moot.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If we look to paragraph 68 of your witness statement, you say: "There was an operation in early September," namely the operation to go to the canal. You describe here events occurring between the 4th and the 8th of September. Let me read the statement -- the paragraph in full. "The operation in early September 1998 I referred to above was made between the 4th and the 8th of September. The area was full of terrorists. The operation had to take place first in order for the MUP to reach the Lake Radonjic." Now, just let's be clear, if we can, please. What operation was it that took place between the 4th and the 8th of September?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the operation carried out by police forces with the SAJ, and as I said I saw that one tank was used while I was present when we were on our way to Lake Radonjic. I went through Prilep via Rznic to reach Lake Radonjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, well, I'll come to your route into the lake in a moment. Can we just have it clear, please, for the record. Is it your testimony that beginning on the 4th and continuing to the 8th of September, there was a Serbian police and SAJ operation to clear the area up to and including the canal? Is that what you're telling us?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. And you mentioned the route that you took to reach the canal, and I think we find this in your witness statement at paragraph 70, that you went there through Prilep and Irzniq. Now, were you with Bekim Kalamashi or Zenelj Alija when you went to the canal for the first time?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Bekim Kalamashi came to the canal. I don't know who brought him there. He may have been with me because I was in the same vehicle as the technicians and the people taking photographs, but I don't think he was in my vehicle. As for Zenelj Alija, he was brought there by others because he was supposed to show some victims -- show the whereabouts of some victims who had been shot and buried near --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness repeat the place, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Sorry, could you repeat the place you were just referring to where Zenelj Alija was supposed to be indicating bodies. The interpreter didn't pick it up.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Zenelj Alija was taken by other operatives to Dasinovac to indicate some places there where some civilians were buried.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. Just so that we're clear, I'm asking you about the very first day you went to the canal. Now, is it your evidence that Zenelj Alija was at the canal or not?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, that was quite far away from the canal. Dasinovac is further away from the canal. It's on the Ratis-Jablanovac road.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So, again, just to be absolutely clear, did Zenelj Alija go to the canal? Was he taken to the canal on the first day, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. I only remember seeing him at Dasinovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You do remember, though, seeing Bekim Kalamashi at the canal, do you?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Bekim Kalamashi showed me the canal.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. And if you just look at paragraph 79 to 80 of your witness statement. In paragraph 80 you suggest that the information given by Kalamashi and Zenelj Alija was video-recorded, and you say this: "This shows them pointing out the specific areas where the bodies were." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see it on the screen, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think it's coming.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It might be quicker if the witness had --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, there's the canal --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- had the paper copy of the statement available to him. I'm asking about 79 and 80 which is on the next page but one.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, looking at paragraph 80, Mr. Zlatkovic, you say there that there is video footage showing Mr. Kalamashi and Mr. Alija pointing out specific areas where the bodies were. Can I ask you this: Have you ever seen footage showing Zenelj Alija or Bekim Kalamashi at the canal?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw Zenelj Alija near Dasinovac indicating that spot.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, I understand that and we've seen that piece of footage as well. The question I'm asking you is: Have you ever seen any footage of Bekim Kalamashi or Zenelj Alija at the canal?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not at the canal.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, just focusing on Mr. Kalamashi, what was it that caused you to say in paragraph 80 of your witness statement that there was a video which showed them, that is the two of them, pointing out specific areas where the bodies were found? What made you say that if you've never seen a video of Mr. Kalamashi at the canal?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw a video of Zenelj Alija. I'm sure that Bekim Kalamashi was also filmed, but I never saw the video. Bekim Kalamashi came to the canal and showed where the executions had taken place.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But you've not managed to see that captured on any of the videos that have been shown to you, Mr. Zlatkovic, have you?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't shown that footage, but I'm sure it exists.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just to be clear about it, I mean, you would expect, wouldn't you, that to be one of the most important pieces of footage because the reason for taking those men there was to show the world that it was they who had led you there; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you repeat your question. I didn't understand it.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Zlatkovic, the reason for taking Mr. Kalamashi to the canal was so that you could demonstrate to the world that it was he who had pointed out the bodies; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not to show the whole world, but for him to show us where to find those people because their families had been searching for them for a long time.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But being realistic about it, Mr. Zlatkovic, you knew where the canal was, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did, but we weren't sure. We thought we might be set up, that someone might inform the terrorists we were coming and they might kill us there.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You told us yesterday that there was an armed Serbian check-point in the village of Irzniq from the 12th of August right up until your visit in September, and Irzniq police station runs right next to the canal, does it not?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, not right next to it. If someone wants to kill you, they can do it five steps away from a police station, ambush you there and kill you.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The route you took through Prilep and Irzniq, you have now seen a piece of video footage and you indicate, I think, in your witness statement that you believe your visit to the canal was on the 8th. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: As you were driving through Prilep and Irzniq, did you notice any VJ forces there?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only that tank I mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And where was that single tank that you noticed?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I was near the canal, it arrived from the direction of Rznic and passed by the cherry orchard and went off I suppose in the direction of Ratise.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: See, Mr. Zlatkovic, we've heard evidence in this court from the British Military Attache to Belgrade who took the same route on the same day that you took through Prilep and Irzniq. And what he saw was a combined force involving the VJ, the MUP, the PJP, and the SAJ approximately 300 or so forces in the area burning properties, burning haystacks, looting houses, and firing randomly at people's properties without any return fire. Did you see any of that, Mr. Zlatkovic?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see that. I didn't see that. I'm sure there was fighting because the forces went through first and then we arrived, but we were not going to fight. In war, all technology is used.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, what did you see when you went through Prilep, just describe it for us, please.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there were houses that had been destroyed or semi-destroyed, but that had been going on for months, that fighting. So I can't say who destroyed them. I didn't participate in that. My only task was to carry out the on-site investigation, nothing else, and who it was that did burning and looting, I'm sure there were people on both sides who did that because when there's a war on there are casualties on both sides and there's damage on both sides.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did you see properties on fire on your way through Prilep and Irzniq?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Anyone could see that, sir. Anyone could see that, journalists went through, the diplomatic mission saw that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Exactly. And did you see a combined VJ and MUP force of 300 people approximately?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were various uniforms around at the time. They had received some new uniforms, camouflage uniforms, those members of the PJP. As for the army, the only thing I saw belonging to the army was one tank. But I can tell you that there were attacks by terrorist groups on Decani and some villages near Decani were burned then. In Decani, a policeman sitting on the road was seriously wounded. There was an attack like that carried out by terrorist groups.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: When you got to the canal, Mr. Zlatkovic, you tell us in your witness statement at paragraph 81 that the area around the lake, and maybe for a number of kilometres, was secured by uniformed police officers from this first visit onwards 24 hours a day. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So if we take the area where the concrete canal ends, are you saying that for an area of several kilometres around that position the MUP maintained control?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: During this anti-terrorist action that was carried out, they were securing that area. They were securing that area because corpses had to be found. So the police were securing the area up to Lake Radonjic from the very beginning of the canal to Lake Radonjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And did that include the economic farm area?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But that was under Serbian control from the 8th of September onwards?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you. Did you see international representatives and media representatives --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The witness used yesterday a different word and we also find it in the statement "Perparimi farm" or something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we just make sure that economic farm is the same as the farm --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The farm that you're referring to when I use the expression "economic farm," is that the place where a body was found whilst you were there?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's a cooperative. It's called Perparimi in Albanian. In Serbian the name is Bratstvo.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But just to be clear, that is the economic farm where a body was found whilst you were on site?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In front of the farm, yes. The building of the farm.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, now, there's one aspect of your evidence in relation to this search operation that I just want to focus on with you, if I may. Can you look, please, at paragraph 91 of your witness statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps before we do so, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'd like to be very sure -- no, that's taken out. Not, the Perparimi farm is usually 175 but that's now out. But if you're talking about the economic farm and the Perparimi farm, is that the same for you, Mr. Zlatkovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perparimi is a cooperative which was in charge of that farm. It's a broad area where sour cherries and hazelnuts are planted. It's a huge area. The cooperative itself also had stables and cow-sheds, and the name of all that was Perparimi, and the farm was part of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And -- yes, and Ekonomija farm was part of that, you said. Is that correctly understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If you can just turn to paragraphs 90 and 91 of your witness statement, Mr. Zlatkovic, please, the document you've got open in front of you, could you find paragraphs 90 and 91, please. Mr. Zlatkovic, could you find paragraphs 90 and 91 of your witness statement, please, on the paper version you have in front of you. Now, you describe earlier in your statement --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is already on the screen at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You described earlier in your statement arriving, you believed, on the 8th; then on the following day meeting the investigating judge there on the 9th. And then at paragraph 90 you pick up events that took place the next day, on the 10th. And you say this: "On the following day, I came again to the canal area. I believe it was the 10th of September, I'm not sure. It was less rainy, but the water flow in the canal increased due to the water coming from the Streoc mountains. "We tried to locate more bodies. We found bodies in the woods above the canal on the right side, looking towards Lake Radonjic, and in the canyon and one body at the farm. We also found some bodies in Dashinoc [sic]." You then deal with a plan at paragraph 92, and at paragraph 93 you say: "I think it was on the same day, I think -- I don't remember exactly. On the same day we found some bodies in Dashinoc [sic]." Now, I just want to be clear about this. In paragraph 91 you speak about finding bodies in the woods above the canal on the right side looking towards Lake Radoniq and in the canyon and one body at the farm. Now, it appears from your statement, Mr. Zlatkovic, that you are indicating that these bodies were found on the 10th; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this case, I couldn't recall the precise date when this happened, but I know that on the 10th the investigating judge arrived and we carried out an on-site investigation, and we set out from in front of the farm, or rather, the Perparimi cooperative, the cow-sheds, and in the sewage channel we found a body. The head was facing west. The hands were raised behind the head --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- the jacket was --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry to interrupt you. I don't want to take time on the details of the body that's found in the drainage canal. I'm asking you about the bodies that you refer in the same sentence to having been found in the woods above the canal on the right side looking towards Lake Radoniq. Now, you would agree, I imagine, that it appears from your statement as though those bodies were found on the same day as the body was recovered from the farm?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Dutertre.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, the witness said that he didn't remember exact dates when it happened. So this is line 9, page 33.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, I'm grateful to Mr. Dutertre for seeking to come to the witness's aid, but I seek to cross-examine and probe his evidence in respect of this matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But at the same time, Mr. Emmerson, if the witness says already in his statement, not only now in cross-examination, that he's uncertain about the dates that it does make much sense to -- of course you could seek to find out whether his recollection could assist him in getting better information. But at the same time, going on for the dates forever is not assisting the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It could lead to confusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'll take him, if I may, to a later portion of the statement dealing with the same issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Could you turn to paragraph 112 of your witness statement. And for this purpose, Mr. Zlatkovic, I wonder if I could ask you, please, to turn also at the same time to tab 36 in the brown bundle. What I'd like to do with you is, first of all, if the usher can just take you to tab 36. This is annex 24 to your witness statement, and it's an aerial photograph on which you have marked certain numbers. And it's the sequence that I'm interested in. We could just for your -- to remind you, Mr. Zlatkovic, if you look to your own witness statement at paragraph 105, you will see the passage where you deal with this map. And you say that you've looked at the aerial photograph and you have marked on it "areas numbered 1 to 8 which relate to locations I recall seeing dead bodies on different days during the Lake Radonjic area investigation." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Paragraph 106 you say that on the first day you saw two bodies in the water, and you've marked on the map a figure 1 to show where those two bodies were seen. And you say: "On the same day I saw a number of bodies on the ground along the canal in the" -- and you had marked the position number 2. And we can see that on the map. And you say: "Later on bodies were dug-up in that area," and you've marked that as position number 3. Then at paragraph 107 you say: "On the second day," so that would presumably be the 9th, "I saw the same bodies as the first day at locations 1 and 2 and I also saw a body beside a car at the end of the waterfall, which I marked number 4." And we can see that on the map. "There were other bodies," you say, "I saw alongside the canyon which I numbered 6 and 7." I want to be clear on this, it's a little difficult to see on the map, but you've also marked a number 5 right by the wooded area on the right-hand side of the canal as we look at it. Can you see where you've put the number 5?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Pausing there for a moment. You say at paragraph 108 that you can't recall which day it was you saw those bodies in that position, and you say they were found by Dragan Stojanovic. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dragan Stojanovic and the group of policemen with him, but I said here, sir, that I cannot recall precisely, and I said that in my statement, whether it was here because I can't see where the farm is here or whether it's where I marked the spot with a number 8 or 9 or something like that. There was a woman here and a man who was in a sack. The woman was completely naked except for a pair of black sandals on her feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, we'll come back to what you actually --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In order to have matters perfectly clear on the record. The marking of number 5 is not easy to detect. May I take it that you and the witness - and I'm also addressing you, Mr. Zlatkovic - when you talked about number 5 that you were talking about the marking made exactly to the right of where we find number 6 at the edge of a wooded patch there where it becomes cultivated land again? Is that where you located the 5? Mr. Zlatkovic, could you follow me or -- I'm still talking about annex 24 --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, I understand you completely. And I will mark it again with a number 5. It's on the edge of the road.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You don't have to mark it again, but I just want to be sure that whomever later reads the transcript of this hearing can find number 5. So it was correct that it is to the right of the marking of number 6 where the wooded -- small wooded area again transforms into cultivated land. Is that the place you are pointing at?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, as I understand it, Mr. Zlatkovic, your testimony is that you're now not sure whether you saw any bodies in that location; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot be specific as to whether the bodies were found precisely there. I did see the bodies myself. There was several of them, a naked female body with just black sandals and a male body which was in a sack.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, let me just be clear about this. Can you help us as to what 9 and 8 are meant to indicate, just for clarity, please?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Number 8 indicates location where we found a jaw, a jaw and a human skirt. Number 9, as I have stated, I can't see whether this is the farm or not so I marked this, meaning to say that it's possible that it was by number 9.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. Can we then look at paragraph 112 of your witness statement, please, and I just want to be absolutely clear what it is you are telling us about those two bodies that you say that you saw. You say at paragraph 112: "At location 5, I was with Veselin Vesovic, Nebojsa Avramovic, and Ljubica Djordjevic. I don't remember if there was anyone else there at that time. I remember seeing two bodies at this location, one of which was in sacks which were placed on the torso and legs. It was naked, except for the black sandals on the feet. The other body was female and was, I think, a complete body." Now, pausing there for a moment. You indicate here that you saw two bodies. Can I be clear, was it you who discovered them or had someone else found them first?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. A policeman found them, and I came and ordered to conduct an investigation with the technicians, because the policemen were the ones who searched the terrain initially.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. And just to be clear, in the area where you saw these two bodies, there were two bodies not three; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two bodies. There were two bodies. Later on --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Dutertre.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you be more specific. Are we speaking about the location where there were the two bodies? Was it the very location or was it a wider area? Could the questions be more focused, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You describe location number 5 in paragraph 112 as a location at which you found two bodies or saw two bodies that had been found by others. The question I'm asking you is: At location number 5 were there two bodies or could there have been three?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say that it was at location number 5. I marked another location. I'm not familiar with this terrain. It's been a long time and I can't tell now whether this was the farm or not. There were some cherry trees there. This is why I marked another location with a number 9, meaning that it might have been there. There were two bodies, however.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: That's the critical question. At this finding, at this site that you're describing, you saw two bodies, not three?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw two bodies there.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, your statement --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, I'm looking at the clock.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I don't know whether this would be --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It's certainly as convenient a moment as any, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then perhaps first. Mr. Zlatkovic, we'll have a break for approximately half an hour. We would like to see you back again after the break. Madam Usher, could you already escort Mr. Zlatkovic out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: How much time would you still need?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No more than 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No more than 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Harvey, how much time would you need?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I think about half an hour, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Maybe 40 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Approximately the same.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. May I take it that Defence counsel -- Mr. Emmerson, you took quite some time --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- to wrap up and such a time that the time asked for by Mr. Harvey and Mr. Guy-Smith are still fitting in the next session.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That means that you might have to take a little bit less and other counsel are encouraged to be as concise and as efficient as possible. We'll have a break until 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we continue, a few practical matters. The Chamber grants the request for testimony to be given by videolink for Witness 10, not pseudonym 10, but 10 order of appearance. Since that's a rather urgent matter, I already give now the decision, the reasons to follow. That's one. The Chamber is still considering annexes 4 and 10, and at least, Mr. Dutertre, looking at annex 4, this is a document, criminal charges brought against the person. Now, I think it's general knowledge that bringing charges against someone, you would usually not do that without having reason to do that, but these are charges, nothing else. At the same time, if you look at the third page, Mr. Dutertre, I read: "From the aforementioned, there is a reasonable doubt that unidentified terrorists have performed the criminal act terrorism to the detriment," and then the persons mentioned. In a criminal charge, as a matter of fact, I would expect that there are reasonable reasons to believe or reasonable reasons to suspect rather than that there are reasonable reasons to doubt. A reasonable doubt is not usually a basis on which you charge a person. So would you please verify whether this is really the document you would like to have admitted, and perhaps whether there's any translation issue. And that's one. Then on annex 10, Mr. Emmerson, you have used that document -- well, not extensively, several portions you used to cross-examine the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Therefore now to say it's not admitted, and have all the cross-examination in. At the same time, the document gives more or less a summary of what the opinions were formed at that time on the basis of unspecified investigations, to say it broadly. That's how the Chamber will consider it, not more and not less. I don't know whether the objection against admission, also in view of the extensive use made of this document during cross-examination stands, because then we would have to take out certain portions.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think it's for Mr. Guy-Smith. It was not my objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If I might, perhaps what would be the best course of action would be if the Defence can have a moment where we can thrash it out among ourselves and we will get back to you with regard to that particular item.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. At the same time you're very much encouraged to do that in the next break --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Understood.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- because Mr. Dutertre is entitled to know what is and what is not admitted into evidence as far as his annexes are concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Understood.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Mr. Emmerson, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Zlatkovic, can we go back to paragraph 112 in your witness statement, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, I earlier noticed that you are now cross-examining on that portion of the 92 ter statement which is not tendered and not -- will not be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Exactly so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Okay, then I take it then that you are operating under Rule 90(H) or --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm -- I'm not specifically operating under any rule, Your Honour. I'm simply cross-examining on the content of a statement made by the witness at this stage. It's not tendered --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- by the Prosecution 92 ter --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But usually --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- and wasn't elicited in chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But if you -- okay. Please proceed. I hear at this moment no objections by Mr. Dutertre, but I'd just like to draw the attention to the fact that we are in -- perhaps not entirely clear what is as far as what exactly the basis of the questions is. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'd like you to look, please, at paragraph 112 of your witness statement, Mr. Zlatkovic. Your hand is resting on it at the moment, I think. All right. Now, in this paragraph you say a number of things I want to ask you about. First of all, you say that when you saw these two bodies you indicate that the body that was in the sacks was naked except for a pair of black sandals on the feet. You told us a little while ago it was the body of the woman that was naked.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. Perhaps there was a misunderstanding. The female body was completely naked with black sandals on the feet, and the male body was in a sack.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, that obviously is something that you recall having been shown some photographs, but look, if I may ask you to, please, at the way that you have written your statement. "I remember seeing two bodies at this location, one of which was in sacks which were placed on the torso and legs. It was naked except for the black sandals on the feet." You agree that your statement indicates that it was the body in sacks that was naked except for sandals on the feet. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most likely there was a mistake in translation. I remember well that the male body was in a sack and the female body completely naked, had sandals on the feet. It's possible that there was a translation error.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Let's just --

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was present there.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Let's just --

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The male body was already decomposing, and one could smell the decomposition process.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, let's just test your suggestion that there's a translation error, Mr. Zlatkovic. If you'd like to look four sentences further down, do you see: "I don't" -- a sentence which reads: "I don't remember the clothing on the female"? Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's possible that something was inserted when the translation was done. I remember the female body. It was quite a large woman and I can describe it now. It's possible that the translators made a mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. So in this paragraph at one point it reads to indicate that it is the man's body that is naked, and at another point it indicates that you don't remember what the clothing was on the woman's body. But you tell the Trial Chamber that you have a completely clear recollection that the woman was naked and the man was clothed. Is that the position we're to understand?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is my position that the female body was naked except for the sandals on the feet. The male body was in a sack.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And then, if I can ask you about this, please, Mr. Zlatkovic. You say: "I was there when the forensic team recovered these two bodies." What forensic team are you there referring to?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dr. Dunjic's and Dr. Aleksandric's teams.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So we can be clear that Dr. Dunjic and Dr. Aleksandric were still at the site when those two bodies were found, on your testimony?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And you saw them because you say: "I was there when the forensic team recovered those two bodies." So you saw those two bodies being recovered by the forensic team; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not the forensic team. I stated earlier that --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, in your questions you're mixing up teams and persons.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. Let me be absolutely clear then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Dutertre.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, if we read that part of the statement that was not submitted under 92 ter, I would rather that we read the portions in their entirety because after the sentence that was read out by Mr. Emmerson we find another sentence that is very clear with regard to the presence of the witness when a forensic team recovered the bodies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, you're invited to --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Put the whole passage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- to have the context included.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm very happy to do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Your statement reads: "I" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You start now reading, Mr. Emmerson, you're aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I am, so I'll do it slowly.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Your statement reads: "I was there when the forensic team recovered these two bodies, and I saw them putting numbers on them but I don't remember the numbers. I didn't see the bodies being removed by the forensic team. I don't remember being at that location for all of the time. I was there when the photographs were photographed." Now, pausing there, Mr. Zlatkovic, the passage I'm asking you about is the sentence which reads: "I was there when the forensic team recovered these two bodies." And you've just told us a moment ago that by "forensic team" you meant Professor Dunjic and Professor Aleksandric. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The witness said, "the team of Professor Dunjic's" --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So please try to identify that. That's a similar observation as -- Mr. Zlatkovic, perhaps you could tell us where you spoke about the team whether the two persons heading the team, Dr. Dunjic and Dr. Aleksandric, were present at that time, one of them, two of them, or none of them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The entire team consisted of four or five physicians and a technician. I can't tell you this in more specific terms. This was nine years ago. The policemen found the bodies. I know both Dr. Dunjic and Dr. Aleksandric because I spent the most time with them out on the field, and I don't know the other members of their team. The policemen found the bodies, pulled them out, and then they were processed by the forensic team. Now, as to who exactly was present, I wouldn't be able to tell you that because that was nine years ago, whether Dunjic was there, whether Aleksandric was there, one of them was present.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. When you say "one of them was present", you mean either Dunjic or Aleksandric; is that your position?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's possible that the third one was there. There was a woman and three physicians.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. So one member of the Belgrade forensic team was present when those bodies were found and recovered; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Processed is what the witness said --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- that's not the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Were processed. Whilst those bodies were still on the site, there was a member of the Belgrade forensic team there?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The bodies were found. It was reported by policemen who conducted the search of the terrain, and then the investigation team arrived together with the forensic experts to look into it.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. I'm going to put the question again until -- maybe my problem -- well, I'm --

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that the question has been put to the witness several times. The witness has said that he had to say. He told us repeatedly that this happened nine years ago. The question is being repeated several times, and I object to this.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I don't know whether we get the same question --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- because I see that the question is not fully answered, at least that's what Mr. Emmerson believes and we will see --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I just want to be absolutely clear so we know what you mean by "processed." Is it your testimony that whilst those two bodies were still at the site where they had been found and before they had been taken away from the area, there was a member of the Belgrade forensic team that saw them on the site where they had been found?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've been repeating my answer, counsel. I've done it several times so far. I don't know what else to tell you. That's all I have to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You haven't, in fact, answered the question that I'm asking you so I'll ask it to you again and ask you to give me a yes or no. Was there a member of the Belgrade forensic team present at the site where those two bodies were found before they were removed, yes or no?
