utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Dutertre --

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection. Not to the fact that the question is put, but then the witness should be given a full picture of what he said about the bodies starting with paragraph 112 up to 114 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, the witness has given already -- there's a rather clear question. Mr. Zlatkovic, that question is whether a member of the Belgrade expert team has been present at the place where the bodies were found before they were removed. That's a rather simple question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, there were a lot of people at the site. There were technicians, there were investigation organs, judges, and among them there was a member of the forensic team.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And -- but again then, was there among all those people, was there a member of the forensic team from Belgrade present at the exact location where the bodies were found before they were removed? Not whether they saw the bodies perhaps at a distance later, but at, they say it in Latin, "in situ," that means at the very location, was there a member of the expert team of Belgrade present, whether with a lot of other people -- just was there anyone present of this team?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, there was.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's a clear answer. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If you would just like to look behind tabs 38 and 39 in the brown bundle, they're immediately after the one you have open. If you can just turn over to 38 and 39, please. Just the other way, Mr. Zlatkovic. Yes. Now, you've been shown these photographs while making your statement, and at paragraph 116 of your statement you indicate that the --

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry. Is it 38, 39 or 37 and 38?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, 37 and 38. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Behind tab 37 are two photographs which you've annexed to your witness statement as annex 25, and at paragraph 116 of your statement you indicate that these photographs show the man in the sack and that you can identify this as the person that you saw. Is that correct? That photograph there, Mr. Zlatkovic.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you're referring to the person who was in the sack, we assumed - at least that's what people said - that it was most probably a policeman who had been kidnapped at Kulina [phoen] Pec of Roma ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Please, listen to the question and answer it, okay. Tab 37 shows two photographs. In your witness statement at paragraph 116 you say that you recognised that photograph as the person that you saw, one of the two people that you saw. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, I don't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: In your witness statement at paragraph 116, you are shown this photograph and you say in terms that these two photographs, of them the top photograph shows the man in the sack that you are referring to at location number 5. Now, is it your evidence that this is the person that you say that you saw as one of the two people described at location number 5?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Now -- and we can see the number 3 there. If you could turn, please, to 38 you then say at paragraph 117, and this is annex 26 to your witness statement, that these two photographs you recognise as being a photograph of the other body that was in that location, a body of a woman. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, if you could, please, turn to tab 6 in this bundle. This is a record compiled by Investigating Judge Cindrak on the 23rd of September, concerning the finding of three bodies in a hazel orchard. Do you see that? Do you have the document?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Perhaps the usher would just help you open the file properly so that it's not inconvenient for you to look at. Thank you. Now, so that we're clear about this, could you help us with the translation of the third paragraph. Could you read the third paragraph out to us, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, usually helping out with the translation is not something that's done through the witness by the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We have an English --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- translation. So if you want to put that to the witness, fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm happy to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Could you look at the third paragraph, please, and at the last sentence of it. Does that indicate where these bodies were found?

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can he have the time to read the entire document so that he knows exactly what we're speaking about, because when the question is put to it as to whether it is at that location that the bodies were found.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Zlatkovic, were you able to read the document? Please proceed, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can you help us, first of all, as to where it is that this records indicates the bodies were found? Look at the third paragraph and the final sentence.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says that two unknown bodies were found, one next to each other, and a third 7 metres further away.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. And we'll look at the numbering in just a moment, but can you look, please, at the third paragraph and the final sentence. Where is it describing those bodies as having been found?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At a distance of 2 and a half kilometres from the village of Rznic along a village road leading by the hazelnut orchard on the left-hand side of the country road. There is a valley where in the bushes bodies were found.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Next to the ravine, 10 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Is this record indicating, Mr. Zlatkovic, as far as you understand it, that these bodies were found 10 metres from the ravine?

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, please. Which ravine are we speaking about? Could we be more specific.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Let me go on what is in the record --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The witness can answer the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Zlatkovic?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have already said that I can't say exactly where this place is because a lot of time has elapsed. On the aerial photograph, I cannot recognise the place. Was it next to the lake or was it further away? I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. My question put simply - if you can't answer it, please say so - is: Does this record indicate that those bodies were found 10 metres from the ravine or canal?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 10 metres from the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. The record is dated the 23rd of September. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And it indicates that the investigating judge - this is the end of the first paragraph - went to the scene with the above-mentioned team and performed an on-site investigation, and you are listed as one of those who attended. Is it the position that you attended with the investigating judge?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And this was on the 23rd of September?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, by that time, Mr. Zlatkovic, there were no members of the Belgrade forensic team present in the area, and according to the evidence of the Belgrade forensic team these bodies were removed before the forensic team had an opportunity to see them. Can you help us about that, please?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's possible they were taken out of that part, out of the ravine.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No, Mr. Zlatkovic, according to the Belgrade forensic team, no member of their team was present or saw these bodies until they were at Hotel Pashtrik. In other words, there was no member of the Belgrade forensic team given an opportunity to see them in situ, because they were removed by the police before the forensic team arrived.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On this point, the consolidated statement of Professor Dunjic provides us with some information. Indeed --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm --

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- I can't go into detail, but he went in situ at a given point in time --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: That's not --

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- and he described what he did --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Dutertre, you can insist that Mr. Emmerson points us to the -- in the question Mr. Emmerson said: "According to the Belgrade forensic team no ..." et cetera. You can ask Mr. Emmerson to give us the source for that so that we are able to verify. If he doesn't give a source or if the source says anything else, I would expect you to object.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. I'm perfectly happy to have the source and the paragraph numbers identified from each of the -- of Professor Dunjic's records. But for the sake of absolute clarity, the evidence of Professor Dunjic is that by the time he returned the bodies had been removed, and there can be no question about that. And whatever Mr. Dutertre might wish at this stage to introduce that is the position on the evidence of Professor Dunjic. He was called back from Belgrade and that by the time he arrived the bodies were in Hotel Pashtrik. I'm happy to have the paragraph number identified. I'm sure Mr. Dutertre is familiar with it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Dutertre.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Quite. That's what he stated, but he added something to the effect that he went in situ. He gave references, and I believe that the counsel failed to see the paragraph where he said that he went on -- in situ.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Not at all. I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Dutertre, if you would like to raise this issue in re-examination, you're perfectly entitled to do so. And Mr. Emmerson has heard that you, at least, fear that he's making a mistake. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. Well just to be absolutely clear, the reason why I laid the foundation that I did with this witness about there being members of the forensic team there before the bodies were removed was specifically because I have it very firmly in mind what Professor Dunjic has to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, I'm want to be clear to you and I'm going to put it to you absolutely clearly, Mr. Zlatkovic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it what he said not what he has to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: What is recorded in his statement. And I'm being handed a note indicating that, yes, just for the record and for Your Honours and Mr. Dutertre paragraph 149 of the consolidated witness statement reads as follows: "The MUP removed these bodies from that location the same day and transported them for forensic purposes to the premises of the garage of Hotel Pastrik." And it was the following day that he was informed and called from Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, I just want to be clear, Mr. Zlatkovic. The evidence of the forensic experts is that their team was not there whilst these bodies were in situ and they were not called until the day after they had been removed. Now, you told us a moment ago there was a member of the forensic team present whilst the bodies were in situ. What is the position, please?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean that Dr. Dunjic might remember? He's older than I am, and maybe he can't recall. He went to Belgrade and back more than once. I was 50 years old at the time and I'm sure my memory was very good. The only mistake is that the forensic technicians should have filmed it, and then we could have shown here who was there and who wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. And was it filmed or photographed?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's what I'm saying. It should have been.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. You can see on this record, Mr. Zlatkovic, that it records three bodies being found, bodies that are numbered 1 and 2 were found immediately together, and body number 3, the body in sacks, was found 7 metres apart. You told us in your evidence that you saw two bodies, not three, and you identified body number 2 that you just looked at a photograph of a moment ago as one of those two bodies. From your recollection, Mr. Zlatkovic, were there three bodies or two?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the best of my recollection there was a woman and a man, who was in a sack. As for the third body, I can't remember it but of course --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you --

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- I have the right to forget something.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. Now, those two bodies that you identified in the photograph, Mr. Zlatkovic, they were subsequently given the labels RE-3 and RE-4. Number 2, that is the woman, was given the label RE-3; and number 3, that is the man in the sack, was given the label RE-4. And we have evidence in this case that RE-3, the woman, was last seen alive on the 6th of September; and RE-4, the man in the sack, last seen alive on the 4th of September being taken into the custody of Serb police in Gjakove police station -- no, I'm sorry, in Gjakove. Now, your evidence as I understand it is that between the 4th and the 8th of September the Serb police were clearing this area. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but I don't know where this information comes from.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have that information available. As I said, my only task was to conduct on-site investigations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, it's of no use to put to the witness where these people were seen last. I mean, that's asking for starting to thinking about what conclusions that would justify. Let's just focus on what the witness can tell us.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. I've got two final topics, if I may, and I'll deal with them briefly.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You gave some evidence in chief to Mr. Dutertre about a man called Isuf Hoxha, and you described him as a poor man who lived on some farm. Where was the farm, please?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the Duvanska Kolonija from Djakovica towards Drin. It's linked to Djakovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. Was it a farm in the countryside?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, they used to grow tobacco there so the people who lived in those sheds called this the Duvanska Kolonija, which means the tobacco colony.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: That's where Mr. Hoxha lived, is it?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: In one of those sheds on the tobacco colony?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And that's where you claimed to have visited him, is it, and seen the photograph on his wall that you told us about?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Once with the chief of the criminal police. He was friendly with him and he went to visit him.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So did you go and visit him there, Mr. Zlatkovic?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was there with Slobodan Kovac, but that was in 1997.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. And where was he living in 1998?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most probably it was there, but I don't know because I only saw him about town but not -- I didn't go there.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. And you told us that he was involved in gambling. Is it correct that he ran an illegal gambling operation?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, every kind of gambling is illegal, let me tell you. Only the state-run gambling enterprises, but everything else is illegal.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And did he get into trouble with the Serb police over this from time to time?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if he was ever brought in because of that, but he would drop in on his own, of his own accord. I would see him standing there, chatting with someone. He had friends there. That man Kovac was a friend of his.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So although he was known to be involved in various kinds of illegal activity, including gambling, he got on well with the Serb police?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think yes, because he went there, I think he did get on well with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Was he paying bribes to Serb police officers, as far as you know?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what he could use to bribe them with. He was a poor man. I think maybe they overlooked his gambling in order to get information from him.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. And finally this, if I may. You gave some evidence about the incident on the 24th of March, 1998, in Gllogjan. Can we be absolutely clear. By the time you arrived, the focus of the exchange of fire had moved away from the area around the Haradinaj compound into the village of Gllogjan; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And you, yourself, never approached the area where the shooting was taking place in Gllogjan?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the first time I entered Glodjane with Milan Stanojevic, he brought me there Slobodan Kovac and some projectiles landed there coming from various sides. We were in some of the houses there overlooking Mr. Ramush's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And did you conduct any investigation at all amongst the civilians of Glodjane about what had happened on that day or did you base your investigation solely on what police officers told you?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The police officers did bring some people and paraffin gloves were taken to see whether they had fired shots. These were Albanians for the most part. They didn't say anything, and all this was based on what the police officers said. What was certain was that this one policeman was killed and that there were wounded on both sides as well as people killed on both sides because people wouldn't say anything, quite simply.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Zlatkovic, we have seen in this case, and it's been admitted into evidence at the request of the Prosecution, a report conducted by an organisation -- published by an organisation called the Humanitarian Law Centre into the events -- amongst other things, into the events of the 24th of March, which records that amongst those arrested a number of the witnesses who were arrested by the police described being beaten. Were you present whilst people were being interviewed after the 24th of March?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't present, but I know that some were released right away, immediately, and others were released in the morning. It was mostly the state security who worked with them. I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. And the Humanitarian Law Centre inquiry also records that whilst some witnesses believed that the police patrol had been shot upon, others said that the patrolmen fired first. Did you ever make any inquiries of the civilian witnesses as to who shot who first in the course of this incident, other than the account that you received from Momo Stijovic?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't talk with those people because I didn't see them again. Even if someone had wanted to answer a summons, he wouldn't dare come.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, I'm -- remember what you said --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm happy to conclude my cross-examination at that point. The document from which I was putting extracts from the witness is Exhibit P6, the "Spotlight" report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. I'm working from left to right, so Mr. Harvey you're now in this position, you're the second one, unless you have arranged that you would take another sequence.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I'm happy either way, Your Honour. Mr. Guy-Smith was going to go next, but I don't mind working --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: All right, fine, if that's what you expected, then Mr. Guy-Smith is --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm amenable.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's start. You'll now be cross-examined, Mr. Zlatkovic, by Mr. Guy-Smith, who is counsel for Mr. Balaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Mr. Zlatkovic, when you were at the Haradinaj compound on the 24th of March, you received information from a gentleman whose name is Zoran Djordjevic; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And Zoran Djordjevic was a member of the State Security Service and he worked under the auspices of Mr. Janisevic [phoen], the chief of SUP in Pristina; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's a mistake. Zoran Djordjevic is a policeman who was assistant commander at the police station in Djakovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Mr. Djordjevic worked with two other police: Dragan Jasovic and Momcilo Sparavalo, did he not?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know those people at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Very well. When you say you don't know these people at all, are you telling us that you've never heard their names before or that you never worked with them or know of anybody else who has worked with them?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I truly don't know who these people are. There were a lot of policemen there, a lot of people passed through the SUP buildings in Djakovica and Decani. I had no contact with those people.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now, you worked for both SUP and MUP, did you not? Is there --

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And during 1998, the period that we've been discussing, from March through September, which one of those organisations or groups were you working with?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As a crime inspector for homicide and sexual assaults, I covered the area of Djakovica and Decani. When the events of 1998 began, or rather, they began in late 1997, my task was broadened to include terrorism and perpetrators of terrorist crimes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And when your duties broadened, as you've put them, to include terrorism and perpetrators of terrorism, at that time you were working with MUP; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you referring to the MUP of Republic of Serbia or the one of Pristina?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That's correct -- of Pristina, of Pristina.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right. I simply sent dispatches on my action taken on the ground. I sent it to the Pristina MUP and they, in turn, forwarded it to Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... It's fair to say that during this period of time, MUP and SUP and the State Security Service were all working together compiling information to deal with, as you've told us, terrorist issues; right?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. Now, in your statement when you first learned about, as you've put it, terrorist issues in 1997, you were told by soldiers, as you've told us at paragraph 16, that Albanian farmers were the terrorists; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I think in 19 -- well, let us not argue about the date, I'm not sure. I think it was late in 1997 or early in 1998, in January. There was a bus travelling between Pristina and Djakovica. There were two or three soldiers on that bus.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... the question is very simply this: You were present when a statement was made that the terrorists were armed Albanian farmers; correct, farmers?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely so. That's how they described those people, that they wore typical shoes called opanci worn by farmers.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... terrorists, you equate that term at all times with people who were members of the KLA, correct? And that's what you've told us at paragraph 18 of your statement?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Could you tell us, please, what information you had to assert, as you do at paragraph 42 of your statement, that in September Albanian terrorists had taken off their uniforms and mixed with the villagers?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Would you please repeat that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Surely. Could you tell us, please, what information you had to assert, as you do in paragraph 42 of your statement, statement that you made and we've been discussing for the past days, that in September Albanian terrorists had taken off their uniforms and mixed with villagers?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When the group with Kalamashi was brought in, they all wore track-suits. The second group, when they surrendered weapons in Donji -- or rather, in Istinic --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- when they were surrendering weapons, the older people waited for the policemen and a large group of young people with sun-tan were all in track-suits, based on which we concluded that they were the KLA fighters or terrorists, as they were referred to at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Major -- excuse me. That's information that you received from Major Milic, which is reflected I believe --

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And Major Milic told you that captured members of the DTS sabotage and terrorist forces were wearing civilian clothes and were armed with long weapons; right?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They allegedly discarded uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Do you know a gentleman who was a police officer with MUP by the name of Milovan, last name is Cimesa, I could be pronouncing it incorrectly, C-i-m-e-s-a, who was a deputy platoon commander and had as an assignment the control of the roads of Pec-Gjakove?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know him.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Mr. Cimesa says in a statement that he gave to the Office of the Prosecutor, recently received by the Defence - and I'm referring to 6 -- U0156871 for the benefit of counsel, paragraph 10 - "however, we never got to see the KLA terrorists, but it must be said that 1998 most of the KLA fighters did not wear uniforms, so it was difficult, if not impossible, to distinguish them from ordinary civilians." Do you agree with that statement, sir?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not that there were no people in uniforms. There were definitely several terrorists whose names I don't have now, but you can find it in the OTP documents, who had been arrested in Crnobreg and some other locations wearing uniforms and then under their uniforms they had track-suits.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... do you agree with Mr. Milovan Cimesa, a deputy platoon commander of MUP, that 1998 most of the KLA fighters did not wear uniforms, so it was difficult, if not impossible, to distinguish them from ordinary civilians, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, no, Mr. Guy-Smith --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I agree with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This answer doesn't assist the Chamber in any way.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Very well. If it doesn't assist --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Why not? Because you asked the witness to say yes or no. First is: Was it that they, the majority, wear or not wear uniforms; and the second is whether it was difficult to distinguish them from civilians which could be done by other matters. So a simple yes or no on this composite question is really not what we are seeking.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, then, I do apologise as I want to help you out.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Do you agree with the statement?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. When the people were arrested on September 3rd, there were a number of individuals who were brought to the police station for questioning; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You've mentioned a couple of those names, I believe, one was Zenelj Alija, another was Bekim Kalamashi; right?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Also brought to the police station was Hashim Alija, Riza Alija, Isa Alija, Agron Alija; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were a lot of people. I knew the two that my team worked with, but there were more of them, not just five or six, more of them. Some were released right away and some were kept in order to conduct an interview.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: The names I've just mentioned, those were people who were also brought to the police station for questioning at that time. They may not have been working with your specific team, but they were also brought to the police station at that time; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Also brought to the police station was Naser Kalamashi, Arben Alija, Ismail Turaku, Enver Turaku, Gani Zeku, Hazir Kalamashi, and Haxhi Alija; right?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, there were several people. I don't know their names except for the two I mentioned, Bekim Kalamashi and Zenelj Alija.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Did you receive information in your capacity as an inspector of homicides that two people at least were killed in Kodralija village by Serbian troops, and that would have been Hashi Alija and Halil Alija?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was fighting there, at least that's what the policemen said.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, in your --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith, are you referring to what -- in early September was a recent event or any longer period of time?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: No, in early September at the time --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: On that time?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes, at that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: When you were obtaining information about what happened at the village of Kodralija, you've told us they were fighting, which I understand. Did you get any information and make any determinations about what Albanians, if any, were killed and whether they were civilians or, as you term them, terrorist fighters?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The only information I have is that they were ambushed outside of the village. There was a patrol of ten people. They opened fire and a conflict erupted. Nobody informed me. It's possible that their superiors were informed, and I was not their superior. They had their own commanders, deputy commanders, and assistant commanders. It's possible that they were informed. If they knew that somebody was killed, they had to write a report.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... whether or not Albanian citizens, I mean -- by that I mean non-fighters, were killed, were beaten by Serbian participants in this fighting be of importance to you in your capacity as a senior police officer who was investigating homicides and terrorist activity?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's possible that something was concealed from me. I can tell you that I arrested several policemen in relation to such cases. In Decani a family of Osa [phoen] was killed and I arrested a policeman called Jovanovic and he was convicted and sentenced to 18 years in prison.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Did you arrest anybody in relation to the incident on September 3rd, 1998, where it is reported that a 73-year-old man and a 23-year-old boy were killed by Serbian troops who were not fighting?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not have such information. Whenever there was information, I'm telling you, you can verify that, it's all documented. Two families were killed in Decani and I arrested Jovanovic Slobodan, who was sentenced to 18 years for that crime.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... that you have this information because something could have concealed from you is that you were not the superior commander for those fighting forces so that information, if it went anywhere, went somewhere other than within your line of command; right?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's possible. I was not the commander. I was not these people's superior.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. During the time that you were stationed in the area, were you aware of an information source called the Kosovo Daily Reporter or Daily Reports?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Did you have an opportunity to -- excuse me --

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is it in Albanian? Is it published in Albanian? Because I don't speak Albanian.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Did you have an opportunity to speak with your colleagues who spoke or read Albanian, understood Albanian, such people as -- excuse me. Such people as Vlahovic about the reporting that was being done concerning Serb operations in various parts of Kosovo, and specifically with regard to what happened in the Kodralija village on the 3rd of September?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. Nobody read it out to me or said anything to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: No one ever informed you during the period of time that you were investigating the specific incident that we've been talking about that local activists in Kodralija said that 12 Albanians who were arrested in the village were taken to the Serb police station virtually nude? You never heard that?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I found those people in a kitchen. They were dressed. Now, as to what happened en route, I don't know. There are all kind of savages. It's possible that people mistreated them. But when they arrived at the police station, they were fully dressed. Now, as to what happened en route, whether they were mistreated, I don't know. Everything is possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I take it then you also were never informed that there was information from the same service that such people as Zenelj Alija, Bekim Kalamashi, Naser Kalamashi, to name but a few, had been reported to have been tortured by the Serbs at the police station in Gjakove?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what that amounted to. Nobody beat them or mistreated them in my presence. They signed the statements, and following that they were detained by the investigative judge upon approval of the regional public prosecutor. I think that they were released from prison first they were in Dubrava and then in Nis and then released later.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The translation ends now. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Bekim Kalamashi was a young boy. How old was he, 17? 20?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that he was young, 17 or 18. Let me tell you, there is a doctor in prison. Once somebody is admitted to the prison, a doctor always examines them. If somebody has a doctor's certificate about being tortured --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: During the time that the questioning of these young men was going on, there were other people being questioned at the police station, too, weren't there?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: When you say "it's possible," are you saying to us now that that's something that might have happened or that's something that you know did happen?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that it certainly happened because some people were released immediately once it was established that they had not participated in combat. Some people were held. There were a lot of people working there, state security, other policemen, and so on, and I wasn't informed of everything that was going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... as a matter of fact, you have told us that one of the things that you were doing was you were collecting statements that were being taken of interviews; right?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wrote criminal complaints based on statements that were taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, what you told us earlier today was that you collected all these statements and you wrote criminal reports or expanded criminal reports - and that's at page 8, line 17 - and that's what you did; right?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Criminal complaints or reports are filed based on statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And it makes sense what you were doing was collecting as much information as you could in order to file a comprehensive criminal report; right?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I analysed the information, and based on that I wrote criminal complaints.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And the information that you analysed, Mr. Zlatkovic, came from sources above and beyond that information that you received as a result of the interviews you've talked about so far today, those by Mr. -- that were conducted by Mr. Vlahovic and Mr. Marinkovic [sic]; right?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. The information came from some confiscated material, an order issued by Mr. Haradinaj, military rule-books. There was a lot of information in that material. We translated that. We analysed it, and then we filed criminal complaints.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith, it's now approximately the fifth or the sixth time that you put your next question when the translation has not finished. Now my --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If I move this back I can do it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What wonders me, seeing that this repeatedly happens, I take it that you're listening to the English channel?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes, as opposed to the French, which is what I oftentimes do in order to slow it down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but you're now listening to the English channel, that means that it seems you're more interested in your next question than in hearing the final part of the answer. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You received information as a result of the interview taken by Bogdan Tomas of Ljulj Musaj, did you not?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have never heard of Bogdan Tomas.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Are you -- are you telling us that during the period of time that you were at the police station you never had contact with or discussed issues concerning the canal with Bogdan Tomas from the State Security Service?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know any such man.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact that Bogdan Tomas testified at this very Chamber concerning his involvement in interviewing people, and specifically Zenelj Alija?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. Just a moment, please. Let's clarify this. Maybe he could have --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'd like the witness to finish what he just said. You said: "Maybe he could have ..." Who is "he" and what could he have?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I just wanted to say that maybe this man Bogdan Tomas, whom I don't know, I've never heard of this last name in my life, maybe later on when Zenelj Alija was in prison in Pec or somewhere else, he might have spoken to him, but I have never heard of Bogdan Tomas.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. When you went out to the canal, you saw Zenelj Alija at the canal; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I saw Zenelj Alija in Dasinovac. He indicated the crime scene in Dasinovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: When Zenelj Alija was seen in Dasinovac, he was in custody, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And the person who was watching him was Bogdan Tomas, right, and you know that to be the case?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I certainly don't know that. I can swear by anything you like that I don't know Bogdan Tomas and whether he was watching Zenelj Alija or not. Maybe when he was arrested permission was given from the prison for him to be brought there, maybe it was all done there.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: During the time that you were questioning people at the police station before you went to the canal, who did you speak with from the State Security Services concerning this matter?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Keep any notes?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't have my notepads any more.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: When did you get rid of your notepads, sir?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I retired.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: As an experienced police officer collecting and analysing information, are you telling this Chamber that there are no reports or notes that you forwarded contemporaneously during this investigation to any headquarters or sources concerning the information that you claimed was gathered by all of the various investigative forces involved in this incident?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what you say. Officially, everything is in Belgrade, probably in the analytics department, but I don't want to keep any personal files nor do I need any.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith, I'm looking at the clock. I'm also rather concerned about -- and I'm not only addressing you but also Mr. Emmerson on the time you took this morning. How much time you would still need?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Not much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Approximately, because I have to decide whether to have a break now or not and then the difference between 7 and 14 minutes is great -- or I should say five and ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Eight.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Eight. Then I'll keep you to that and we'll have a break in eight minutes from now.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'd like to ask you one question with regard to a view of Judge Radomir Jokovic [sic] and see if you share this view. You know who Judge Radomir Jokovic is, correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not Radomir Djokovic but Radomir Gojkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Radomir Gojkovic has stated in a statement made to the OTP that: "The Albanians settle their quarrels by death; it is their rule of nature." Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. Let me tell you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Dutertre.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like to know what the relevance of this question is in this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it that Mr. Guy-Smith is seeking to find out about the attitude of this witness on certain matters, but whether he has to agree with another person, yes or no, on this respect, a direct question would have done as well, Mr. Guy-Smith. I'm ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- not interested in the answer to the question. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: With regard to the type of activities that you were investigating, which I believe are similar to the type of activities that the judge was investigating, would it be fair to say that the most common type of crime as you would characterise it that you had to deal with was the charge of persons coming together to take part in hostile activities for terrorist crimes?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me just a moment. Let me focus on this. Could you repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes. The activities you were investigating which are similar to the activities and type of activities that the judge who we were just referring to was investigating, was the charge of persons coming together taking part in hostile activities for terrorist crimes?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I don't have an answer. I don't have an answer. I don't know if you do. I don't know if any translation --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The witness said: "Joining," but it was not clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your answer to this question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Precisely so. In a Yugoslav criminal law there is a crime of conspiring for criminal activity, and this also includes terrorism. And Radomir Gojkovic said, I agree with it, because that's what it says in the criminal code, the Yugoslav Criminal Code, which is today the Serbian Criminal Code.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: In the activities that you were investigating were such things as the digging of trenches, the supplying of food, or the joining together of groups of people who had a disagreement with and wished to be free from Serbian rule; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct because that's what the criminal law envisaged, and we were only a service which was supposed to enforce that. And who joined together with who, that was well-known --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm not sure --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- who conspired with whom.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: -- how many minutes I have left and I don't want to abuse them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You have two minutes left.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Two minutes left.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: During your compiling of information, did you receive a criminal report on September 6th from Rade Vlahovic concerning his personal circumstances?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Through the duty service, a criminal complaint was filed concerning his parents going missing.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And on September 6th, did you also receive a criminal complaint from Mr. Radunovic?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Radunovic also filed a criminal complaint on the 6th of September about his parents going missing and allegedly his house being looted.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have both of those documents released available in the system, which I would like the witness -- I have them in English and they also are in Serbian. I have the Serbian at this point in hard copy --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Are they uploaded in the system?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: They are uploaded in the system, I have two copies, hard copies, in Serbian and I have it uploaded in English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Madam Registrar, that --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That would be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The first one would be about Mr. Vlahovic --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Vlahovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- And that would be number ...?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: 729 -- 2D00729 in the system the second one is 2D00731 in the system.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, the first one about Mr. Vlahovic would be number ...?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be Exhibit Number D148, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And the other one, that is the document in relation to Mr. Radunovic would be ...?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The next one would be Exhibit Number D149, for -- marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Mr. Zlatkovic, did you have a chance to take a look at those two documents?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I read them even before this.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: With regard to the first document D148, is that the report that was filed?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes this is it, and Rade Vlahovic filed a criminal report with the SUP of Djakovica, saying that his parents were missing and that his house had allegedly been looted.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The second document, Ljubisa Radunovic also filed a criminal report, saying that his parents were missing and that allegedly his house had been looted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Last question, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Those two documents that we've just discussed, that is the first time that reports were filed concerning these incidents; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Allegedly Rade Vlahovic and Ljubisa Radunovic, as they were both policemen and their brothers were probably in the reserve police force, were unable to visit their villages so they couldn't check whether their parents were alive or not. After this action, they found that their parents were missing, and that's why they submitted these criminal reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll have a break. Is there -- these are not the usual documents. I take it that you want to tender them?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I will, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Is there any objection against these two documents? No. Then they are admitted into evidence. Mr. Guy-Smith, I can imagine that I said your last question that it's not a very satisfactory way of concluding, unless this is just what you wanted to establish. Of course we haven't seen yet the dates of those documents, therefore we do not know how surprising it is that in relation to the events that they were filed at that moment, not any earlier, not any later. If that is what you're aiming at and if that was your last issue, then after the break I'll give you two minutes more to establish what you want to establish.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps in view of some of the other questions, it might have been wise to come with these questions first and to ask about focus on terroristic activities at a later stage --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Only what happened was that I reversed my pile.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, take care that it doesn't happen again. We'll have a break for 20 minutes until ten minutes past 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith, the 120 seconds start now. If you come right to your point --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm going to ask the date of the document; I'm going to sit down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Mr. Zlatkovic, do you still have before you the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you just want to establish the date of the document, it's now in evidence, we can read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, that was my feeling beforehand, but since you mentioned the issue of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, I didn't know --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Fine --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm stopping now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That was the most effective use of 30, 40 seconds we've ever made --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Zlatkovic, you'll now be further cross-examined by Mr. Harvey, who is counsel for Mr. Brahimaj. Please proceed, Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Mr. Zlatkovic, we don't have much time, I'm going to come to the point quickly. I want to ask you some questions about Jabllanice and what you believed to be a KLA stronghold in Jabllanice. You understand me?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: In addition to documents that you recovered from houses and various locations, one of the most important sources of information for your investigations was speaking to what you called "loyal Albanians". Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not just I. Everybody called them loyal Albanians.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Well, what did -- what do you mean by the expression "loyal Albanians"?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, what I meant by the expression "loyal Albanians" was people who did their jobs, who did not rise up against the authorities, the Serb police, the army, the officials, and so on and so forth. They paid their taxes regularly, didn't cause any damage, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: People who were opposed to the KLA, for one thing?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: People who were helpful to the police in letting you know about the movements or suspected movements of KLA members?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely so, but not all Albanians did that. There were people who were peaceful, they did their jobs, they worked in their factories, ran their private businesses, and simply did not get involved in politics. They weren't interested in politics. They just did their jobs.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: One source of information was through the families of police officers and police reservists; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and individual policemen who didn't want to leave in the 1980s when almost all the Albanians left their jobs in the civil service or state services. They lived in villages, had family connections, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: You also got information from poor people like Isuf Hoxha, right, people for whom the police did favours?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mentioned Jusuf Hoxha as a poor man, but there were also wealthy Albanians who had strong enterprises and who gave information. For example, some businessmen in Djakovica, some businessmen in Pec, some businessmen in Decani. That was the area I covered. They also provided information because they complained that people from the KLA were asking them for money to obtain weapons, ammunition, and so on. That's how we got information also.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: During the period of 1998, the police also made use of loyal Albanians to whom they gave weapons to contribute to local security, as it was put?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: So these were --

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But that's done in all countries.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: These were -- I'm not talking about police officers or reservists; I'm talking about civilians to whom the police gave weapons, yes?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we misunderstand each other. What I'm saying is that everybody gives weapons to individuals who ask for them because that's all the police can do for them, and then later on they do favours.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: One family for -- that did favours to the police from time to time was known as the Jakupi family. Do you remember the Jakupi family?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Mushk Jakupi, do you remember him?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, an elderly man.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And he had quite a large family who were all known to help the police from time to time?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. They were in the local police force.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Some were in the police force and some were just civilians who were helpful to the police; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Now, when you obtained information from informers, from people like Isuf Hoxha or the Jakupi family, how was that information recorded? Did you take statements or did you simply make reports?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they were registered informants, as we called them associates. They exist everywhere in the world.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Of course they do. And you maintained a register, as you put it, of informants; right?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't have such people in Kosovo because I didn't speak Albanian; however, I received information from my colleagues who spoke Albanian and who cooperated with them. I only knew those people by sight.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I apologise, the English language is poor in this respect. You -- by "you," I meant plural, you, the Serb police, the MUP. Now --

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, but let me give you an example. One person contacted one registered informant, not ten policemen. One policeman would gather information from one source, and then that was registered and used in further operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: In addition to a register of the names of the informants, there was presumably also a register of money paid to informants; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that. I wasn't in charge of that, and in my 40 years of service I was never given money to distribute to our registered informants. I was dealing with homicide, and there was no money to give out there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: You were dealing with what you referred to as terrorism, and one of the aspects of investigating terrorism is that many members of the general public are reluctant to speak to the police when the police question them. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand you. Could you repeat it, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Well -- perhaps it's self-evident. I'm not going to pursue that because of the time. I want to ask you about a particular person, and I want to ask you in relation to paragraph 29 of your statement where you say -- you refer to people being kidnapped and taken to camps at Jabllanice or Gllogjan, and you say that you learned information about this from people who escaped and that statements were taken from them in Gjakove. Do you recall making -- you recall that in your paragraph 29 of your statement?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sometime in July, I think it was July. A large group of people were kidnapped from Orahovac. Those people were kept in Jablanica. Some of them fled from Jablanica and came to the Djakovica SUP. Then they said that there were camps, and another person who told us about the camps was Bekim Kalamashi.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: You refer to statement being taken at SUP Djakovica. Apart from Bekim Kalamashi -- apart from Bekim Kalamashi and Zenelj Alija, are you aware of other statements taken at Djakovica about Jabllanice?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that somebody interviewed them, the policemen did. These people were hungry, they were taken to the kitchen and fed there. And then somebody interviewed them. Now what happened to those statements afterwards, whether they were assessed as useful or not, whether they were given to the prosecutor's office and what happened to them afterwards, I truly don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I want to ask you about one particular individual --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And for this we need to go into private session for just one moment, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We turn into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Have you heard of the person whose name I just gave you, Witness 6?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know him. Judging by the name, I would say that he was a Catholic Albanian, but I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Well, if that's a guess, sir, it's a good one. On the 25th of July of 1998, he has told this Tribunal on that date he left Jabllanice, and between the 25th and the 30th of July, 1998, he spoke with Mr. Camovic at the Pashtrik Hotel in Gjakove. First of all, sir, do you -- did you ever from time to time have coffee together with Mr. Camovic in the Pashtrik Hotel?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never, or rather, let me tell you this. On the 14th of May, 1999 -- I left Djakovica on the 15th of May, and before I left, the evening before, I had coffee with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: As for July of 1998, you didn't socialise with Mr. Camovic?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was chief of state security and I was an ordinary operations officer. He was much, much higher than I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Were you aware that he had information about Jabllanice?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that, but most likely he did have that information because I saw him socialising with Albanians.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Did you provide Mr. Camovic with information about Jabllanice?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Unless he received the information that we had obtained from Bekim Kalamashi. As for me informing him personally, no, that wasn't possible. All I knew about Jablanica came from Bekim Kalamashi, and I also heard about it from policemen once I got there who had told me that five to six years prior to the events it was already impossible for them to go to Jablanica. Now, as to why, I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: In paragraph 31 of your statement you say that the first attempt by MUP to push the Albanian terrorists away from the Djakovica-Pec road towards Jabllanice, Djakovica municipality, and regain control of that road was done on the 2nd of August, 1998. You recall that in your statement, sir?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I want to ask you some -- I want to ask you some questions about that operation. First of all, were you involved in any aspect of that operation yourself, sir?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I personally wasn't involved. I came to Rastavica in order to conduct on-site investigation because the unit had already engaged in combat and in case somebody got killed and if the terrain was liberated, then we would come in to conduct on-site investigation and I just came into one room there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: You did not go to Jabllanice?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: But you are aware that there was a full-scale offensive against Jabllanice on the 2nd of August, 1998, aren't you?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They began with it, but it was halted at around 10.00, I guess. The combat was halted in the area leading towards Decani. What went on there, I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Why do you say it was halted around 10.00? What are you basing that on?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was impossible. Let me tell you, the Albanians were really well-organised and when the police forces moved ahead they descended down some 10 to 20 metres only from the main road. And then the combat was halted and then they came back. I don't know what was happening towards Jablanica, Crmljane, and other locations. In this area here, the combat was aborted, halted.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I'm asking you specifically about Jabllanice on the 2nd of August. Are you saying that MUP forces did not enter Jabllanice on the 2nd of August?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm telling you I don't know. I don't know because Jablanica is far away from Rastavica. I don't have any information about whether they entered or not. It's possible that they did and it's possible that they didn't. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Well, perhaps we could have on the screen your annex -- well, I think you have it in front of you, your annex 7 at page U0167550. Do you have your annex 7 in front of you, sir?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have it here on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: This is the English version, isn't it, Mr. Harvey?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I seem to have the Serb version. Anyway, may I take it that everybody does have in paper form annex 7 if not on the screen before them.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: The relevant page in B/C/S I'm reminded is U0167557, and the part that I want to direct you to, sir, is given the number KU 73/99. Do you have that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's on page 6 of the B/C/S document, the bottom half of the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Do you have the passage now, sir?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Have you found it, Mr. Zlatkovic, at the bottom of page 6 --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's fine, it's fine. I have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Now, it's right to say, isn't it, that whenever -- this -- first of all, this is a report compiled by you, isn't it, if you go over to the next page I think you'll see your signature on this report.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And it's right to say that nowhere in any of these reports do we see that any attack has been carried out by MUP or SUP. Attacks are always recorded as having been carried out by terrorists, aren't they?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And this report was compiled in February of 1999. Why was it compiled so late, so long after the events of the 2nd of August?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was compiled because it was then that they learned that that group had been active there. That was the intelligence they received. Sometimes policemen would go out to patrol, and those patrol groups were reinforced. They had 10 to 15 policemen in them because it was known that terrorists were active in a certain area. Whenever policemen would enter a village, they would open fire and then fighting would erupt and somebody would be killed. That's my explanation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Zlatkovic, it seems that this is not an answer to the question. Mr. Harvey would like to know why a report was only made in February 1999 on events that had taken place already early August 1998.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was then that they learned that the perpetrators of the crimes of terrorism were people listed in a criminal complaint. It was then that they learned when they gathered the information.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Are you seriously suggesting that you didn't commence to gather information about the killing of Zelko Bozic on the 2nd of August, 1998, you didn't begin your investigation until February of 1999?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. They started gathering information right away; however, the names of perpetrators were not known. Later on we learned the names of the organisers of the crime and then we filed a criminal complaint against them.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Well, this is not what we have here a criminal complaint, is it, KU 73/99 or is it? What does "KU" stand for?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It stands for criminal register, KU number, criminal register for crimes that are listed as crimes, they are filed in criminal register. Criminal complaint is filed, is registered, in the criminal register. This is why it was assigned this KU number.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And where is that criminal register today, sir, in Belgrade or Jagodina?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is most likely in Jagodina because SUP Djakovica because relocated to Jagodina.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Jagodina. Thank you for correcting me. Now, you indicated ...

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: You indicated that at around 10.00 on the 2nd of August, the fighting at Jabllanice had ceased, if I understood you correctly. Is that your position, sir?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ZLATKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I apologise. I said that at around 10.00, or perhaps a bit later, I'm not sure of the time, the fighting stopped in the area between Djakovica and Decani, not in Jablanica. Jablanica is in a quite a different place. Jablanica is a -- a surrounded by forests, it's in a valley, and it's I don't know how many kilometres away, but quite a way. It is impossible to hear any firing or any weapons, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I note the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I do have, I'm afraid, this has taken longer than I had anticipated and I have cut a lot of my questions out, but I do have quite a bit more for this witness and he is important to my client's case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: How much time would you still need?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: The way we're going, no less than half an hour, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: But I know Mr. Dutertre has told me --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Dutertre needs another 15 minutes from what I understand. I don't know how many questions there are from the Bench, that means that we'll not finish today. Mr. Zlatkovic, I do hear that you're still available tomorrow, but only in the morning and not very long, but one hour tomorrow. Would that be a possibility?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I just need to make it to Amsterdam for my plane, if I could be assisted in that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- but I'm willing to assist you as much as I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm informed that the time we would need would still allow you to be in time at Schiphol airport. That means that we'll conclude for the day. May I add that the Chamber -- and Mr. Harvey, I'm not specifically addressing you, you're always -- since you're the last, you're always -- of course you might think that you are the one to be blamed, you're certainly not. But the Chamber was not in every respect impressed by the efficiency of today's -- of today's cross-examination. But let's not spend too much time on it. Let's improve for tomorrow. Mr. Dutertre, you're on your feet. Anything to be raised before tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not really, but with respect to annex 4, because a question was put about annex 4, there is a translation error. I've been told that it should read "reasonable ground" and not "reasonable doubt." We'll upload a new version of the document, of the translation, as quickly as possible in the e-court system.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Dutertre, for that. At the same time, everyone, parties included, are invited to detect these kind of mistakes which appear already from the logic itself. Mr. Harvey -- then, Mr. Dutertre, do I understand that 92 bis would be possible, as we discussed earlier the issue of -- the issue of having a officer ready to make the 92 bis attestation rather than to hear testimony through videolink under 92 ter?

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's the way I understand the matter, subject to Mr. Re's correction, I think that we can hear the next witness under Rule 92 bis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I see, Mr. Re, you are nodding yes, so that's confirmed. Mr. Zlatkovic, I again instruct you not to speak with anyone about your testimony, whether already given or still to be given, and we'd like to see you back, tomorrow morning, 9.00 in this same courtroom. We stand adjourned until tomorrow, 9.00, Courtroom III.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 18th day of July, 2007, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.47 p.m.,
